title.zh: 卷391 列傳一百七十八 倭仁 李棠阶 吴廷栋
title.en: Volume 391 Biographies 178: Wo Ren, Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong
title.raw: 卷391 列傳一百七十八 倭仁 李棠阶 吴廷栋

sentences.zh: 倭仁，字艮峰，烏齊格里氏，蒙古正紅旗人，河南駐防。

translations.literal: Wo Ren, whose style was Genfeng, was of the Ujigri clan, a Mongol of the Plain Red Banner, garrisoned in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren, styled Genfeng, belonged to the Ujigri clan—a Mongol of the Plain Red Banner stationed in Henan.

sentences.zh: 道光九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9 (1829) he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 歷中允、侍講、侍讀、庶子、侍講學士、侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He successively served as Junior Censor, Reader-in-Waiting, Expositor-in-Waiting, Junior Tutor, Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, and Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of junior censor, reader-in-waiting, expositor-in-waiting, junior tutor, and both reader- and expositor-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢詹事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to junior mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to be President of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，應詔陳言，略曰：「行政莫先於用人，用人莫先於君子小人之辨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, [Wo Ren] responded to the imperial summons to submit opinions, stating in summary: "In administration nothing comes before the employment of men; in the employment of men nothing comes before distinguishing gentlemen from petty men."
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor took the throne, Wo Ren answered the call for memorials and wrote, in essence: "Governing well begins with choosing the right people, and choosing people begins with telling gentlemen from petty men."

sentences.zh: 夫君子小人藏於心術者難知，發於事蹟者易見。

translations.literal: As for gentlemen and petty men, what is concealed in their inner designs is hard to know; what manifests in their deeds is easy to see.
translations.idiomatic: What gentlemen and petty men keep hidden in their hearts is hard to discern, but what shows in their actions is easy to see.

sentences.zh: 大抵君子訥拙，小人佞巧；

translations.literal: Generally speaking, gentlemen are slow of speech and awkward [in manner], while petty men are flattering and artful;
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, gentlemen are plain-spoken and unadorned, petty men glib and cunning;

sentences.zh: 君子澹定，小人躁競；

translations.literal: gentlemen are calm and composed, petty men restless and contentious;
translations.idiomatic: gentlemen are calm and steady, petty men restless and grasping;

sentences.zh: 君子愛惜人才，小人排擠異類；

translations.literal: gentlemen cherish talent, petty men drive out those unlike themselves;
translations.idiomatic: gentlemen cherish talent, petty men squeeze out anyone unlike themselves;

sentences.zh: 君子圖遠大，以國家元氣為先，小人計目前，以聚斂刻薄為務。

translations.literal: gentlemen plan for what is far-reaching and put the vital energy of the state first, while petty men calculate for the present moment and make harsh exaction and niggardliness their business.
translations.idiomatic: gentlemen look to the long term and put the nation's underlying strength first; petty men fix on the moment and make harsh levies and meanness their trade.

sentences.zh: 剛正不撓、無所阿鄉者，君子也；

translations.literal: Those who are upright and unyielding and curry favor with no one are gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: Those who are upright, unbending, and beholden to no faction are gentlemen;

sentences.zh: 依違兩可、工於趨避者，小人也。

translations.literal: those who waver between two sides and are skilled at evasion are petty men.
translations.idiomatic: those who sit on the fence and excel at dodging responsibility are petty men.

sentences.zh: 諫諍匡弼、進憂危之議，動人主之警心者，君子也；

translations.literal: Those who remonstrate and assist, who advance counsels of peril and alarm and stir the ruler's sense of warning, are gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: Those who speak bluntly to correct the ruler, who offer warnings of danger and stir the sovereign to vigilance, are gentlemen;

sentences.zh: 喜言氣數、不畏天變，長人君之逸志者，小人也。

translations.literal: those who delight in speaking of fate and cosmic cycles, who do not fear heavenly portents, and who foster the ruler's inclination to ease are petty men.
translations.idiomatic: those who talk of fate and omens without dread of heaven's warnings, and who encourage the ruler's taste for ease, are petty men.

sentences.zh: 公私邪正，相反如此。

translations.literal: Public and private, crooked and straight—they oppose one another in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Public duty and private interest, integrity and corruption—they stand opposed in just this way.

sentences.zh: 皇上天亶聰明，孰賢孰否，必能洞知。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is heaven-endowed and penetratingly intelligent; who is worthy and who is not, you must surely see through completely.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is gifted by Heaven with keen insight; who is worthy and who is not, you can surely discern.

sentences.zh: 第恐一人之心思耳目，揣摩者眾，混淆者多，幾微莫辨，情偽滋紛，愛憎稍涉偏私，取捨必至失當。

translations.literal: I only fear that with one person's mind, thoughts, and ears and eyes, those who fathom [your wishes] are many and those who confuse are many; what is subtle cannot be distinguished, truth and falsehood grow tangled, if love and hate slightly involve partiality, choices and rejections will necessarily go wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear that a single mind and pair of ears, however sharp, face a crowd of courtiers guessing your wishes and clouding your judgment—until the subtle is lost, truth and pretense tangle, a trace of favoritism skews love and hate, and appointments go awry.

sentences.zh: 知人則哲，豈有他術，在皇上好學勤求，使聖志益明，聖德日固而已。

translations.literal: "To know men is to be wise"—is there any other method? It lies solely in Your Majesty's love of learning and diligent seeking, so that the sagely purpose grows ever clearer and sagely virtue is daily strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: "To know men is wisdom"—there is no other art: Your Majesty need only study diligently, so that your purpose grows clearer and your virtue firmer day by day.

sentences.zh: 宋程顥雲，'古者人君必有誦訓箴諫之臣'。

translations.literal: Song [dynasty] Cheng Hao said, "In antiquity rulers necessarily had ministers who recited admonitions and offered remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hao of the Song said, "In antiquity every ruler kept counselors who recited lessons and offered frank remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 請命老成之儒，講論道義，又擇天下賢俊，陪侍法從。

translations.literal: I beg that seasoned Confucian scholars be ordered to expound the Way and its principles, and that worthy and eminent men from throughout the realm be selected to attend and accompany [Your Majesty] in the manner of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that venerable scholars be charged to expound the Way, and that the finest minds in the empire be chosen to attend you as moral exemplars.

sentences.zh: 我朝康熙間，熊賜履上疏，亦以'延訪真儒'為說。

translations.literal: In our dynasty, during the Kangxi reign, Xiong Cilü memorialized the throne, likewise urging "the extension of visits to true Confucians."
translations.idiomatic: In our own dynasty, during Kangxi's reign, Xiong Cilü submitted a memorial making the same plea—to seek out true scholars.

sentences.zh: 二臣所言，皆修養身心之要，用人行政之源也。

translations.literal: What these two ministers said are all essentials for cultivating mind and body, and the source of employing men and administering government.
translations.idiomatic: What these two ministers said goes to the heart of self-cultivation—and to the root of appointing officials and governing well.

sentences.zh: 天下治亂系宰相，君德成就責講筵。

translations.literal: Whether the realm is governed or in disorder depends on the chief minister; the accomplishment of the ruler's virtue rests on the lecture seat.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the realm is ordered or chaotic hangs on the chief minister; whether the ruler's virtue matures rests on his teachers at the lecture seat.

sentences.zh: 惟君德成就而後輔弼得人，輔弼得人而後天下可治。

translations.literal: Only when the ruler's virtue is accomplished can the right assistants be obtained; only when the right assistants are obtained can the realm be governed.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the ruler's virtue is formed can he secure worthy ministers; only with worthy ministers can the realm be well governed.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上稱其切直，因諭大小臣工進言以倭仁為法。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised its forthright urgency and thereupon instructed officials great and small to submit opinions, taking Wo Ren as their model.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor praised its blunt honesty and told officials at every level to speak up as Wo Ren had done.

sentences.zh: 未幾，禮部侍郎曾國籓奏用人三策，上复憶倭仁言，手詔同褒勉焉。

translations.literal: Before long, Zeng Guofan, Vice President of the Ministry of Rites, memorialized three policies for employing men; the Emperor again recalled Wo Ren's words and by autograph edict commended and encouraged them together.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Zeng Guofan of the Ministry of Rites submitted three proposals on appointments; the emperor recalled Wo Ren's memorial as well and by personal edict praised both men.

sentences.zh: 尋予副都統銜，充葉爾羌幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was granted the brevet rank of Vice Commander-in-Chief and appointed Assistant Commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the brevet rank of vice commander-in-chief and appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 大理寺少卿田雨公疏言倭仁用違其才，上曰：「邊疆要任，非投閒置散也。

translations.literal: Tian Yugong, Vice President of the Court of Judicial Review, memorialized that Wo Ren's appointment misused his talents; the Emperor said, "A frontier post of importance is not idling him in neglect."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yugong, vice president of the Court of Judicial Review, argued that Wo Ren was being misused; the emperor replied, "A key frontier post is no banishment to idleness."

sentences.zh: 若以外任皆左遷，豈國家文武兼資、內外並重之意乎？

translations.literal: If every appointment outside the capital were treated as a demotion, would that accord with the state's intent to employ both civil and military talent and give equal weight to inner and outer service?"
translations.idiomatic: If every post beyond the capital were treated as exile, how would that square with a state that values civil and military talent alike and weighs inner and outer service equally?"

sentences.zh: 」咸豐二年，倭仁复上敬陳治本一疏，上謂其意在責難陳善，尚無不合，惟僅泛語治道，因戒以留心邊務，勿託空言。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, Wo Ren again submitted a respectful memorial on fundamental remedies; the Emperor said its intent to admonish and present what is good was not inappropriate, but that it spoke only in generalities about the way of governance, and therefore admonished him to attend to frontier affairs and not trust to empty words.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2, Wo Ren submitted another memorial on root remedies; the emperor said his intent to admonish and offer sound counsel was acceptable, but that he spoke only in generalities about governance, and warned him to mind frontier duties rather than indulge in empty talk.

sentences.zh: 候補道何桂珍上封事，言倭仁秉性忠貞，見理明決，生平言行不負所學，請任以艱鉅，未許。

translations.literal: He Guizhen, an expectant circuit intendant, submitted a sealed memorial stating that Wo Ren's nature was loyal and steadfast, his grasp of principle clear and decisive, and that his words and conduct in life did not betray his learning; he asked that [Wo Ren] be entrusted with arduous tasks—[the request] was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He Guizhen, an expectant circuit intendant, submitted a sealed memorial praising Wo Ren's loyalty, clarity of judgment, and conduct worthy of his learning, and asking that he be given heavy responsibility—the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 三年，倭仁劾葉爾羌回部郡王阿奇木伯克愛瑪特攤派路費及護衛索贓等罪，詔斥未經確訊，率行參奏，下部議，降三級調用。

translations.literal: In the third year, Wo Ren impeached Aimait, the Aqimu Beg of the Muslim Department at Yarkand, for crimes including levying travel expenses and his guards' extortion of bribes; an edict rebuked [Wo Ren] for impeaching without thorough investigation, referred the case to the ministries for deliberation, and [he was] demoted three ranks and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Wo Ren impeached Aimait, the Muslim beg at Yarkand, for levying travel fees and taking bribes through his guards; the court rebuked him for accusing without a full inquiry, and after ministry review he was demoted three ranks and transferred.

sentences.zh: 四年，侍郎王茂廕等請命會同籌辦京師團練，上以軍務非所長，寢其議。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Vice Presidents Wang Maoyin and others asked that [Wo Ren] be ordered jointly to organize militia training in the capital; the Emperor, considering that military affairs were not his strength, shelved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wang Maoyin and others asked that Wo Ren help organize capital militia training; the emperor, judging military affairs not his forte, set the idea aside.

sentences.zh: 尋命以侍講候補入直上書房，授惇郡王讀。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered to enter the Southern Study as an expectant reader-in-waiting and to instruct the Prince of Dun in his studies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered into the Southern Study as an expectant reader and appointed tutor to the Prince of Dun.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 歷光祿寺卿、盛京禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as President of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice President of the Ministry of Rites at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice president of the Mukden Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 七年，調戶部，管奉天府尹事，劾罷盛京副都統增慶、兵部侍郎富呢雅杭阿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and supervised the affairs of the Fengtian prefect; he impeached and secured the dismissal of Zengqing, Vice Commander-in-Chief at Mukden, and Funiyehang'a, Vice President of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he moved to the Ministry of Revenue and oversaw the Fengtian prefecture; he impeached and brought down Mukden vice commander Zengqing and War Ministry vice president Funiyehang'a.

sentences.zh: 及頒詔中外，命充朝鮮正使。

translations.literal: When an edict was promulgated within and without, he was appointed chief envoy to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: When a major edict was issued at home and abroad, he was appointed chief envoy to Korea.

sentences.zh: 召回京，授都察院左都御史。

translations.literal: Recalled to the capital, he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was made left censor-in-chief of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 (1862) he was promoted to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 兩宮皇太后以倭仁老成端謹，學問優長，命授穆宗讀。

translations.literal: The two Empress Dowagers, considering Wo Ren mature, upright, and careful and his learning outstanding, ordered him to instruct the Muzong Emperor in his studies.
translations.idiomatic: The two empress dowagers, finding Wo Ren seasoned, upright, and learned, appointed him tutor to the Tongzhi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 倭仁輯古帝王事蹟，及古今名臣奏議，附說進之，賜名啟心金鑑，置弘德殿資講肄。

translations.literal: Wo Ren compiled the deeds of ancient emperors and kings and memorials of famous ministers past and present, added explanations, and presented them [to the throne]; they were bestowed the title Mirror of the Heart to Open the Mind and placed in Hongde Hall for lecturing and study.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren compiled deeds of ancient rulers and memorials of great ministers, with his own commentary, and presented the work; it was named Mirror to Open the Mind and kept in Hongde Hall for the emperor's instruction.

sentences.zh: 倭仁素嚴正，穆宗尤敬憚焉。

translations.literal: Wo Ren had always been stern and upright, and the Muzong Emperor especially revered and stood in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren was famously stern and upright, and the young emperor especially respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 尋兼翰林院掌院學士，調工部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he concurrently served as Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, was transferred to Minister of Works, and was made Grand Secretary without portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added the post of Hanlin chancellor, was transferred to minister of works, and made grand secretary without portfolio.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「河南自咸豐三年以後，粵、捻焚掠，蓋藏已空，州縣誅求仍復無厭。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "Since the third year of Xianfeng in Henan, the Cantonese and Nian rebels have burned and plundered until storehouses are empty, yet the districts and prefectures' exactions remain insatiable."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Since Xianfeng 3 in Henan, Taiping and Nian raids have emptied every granary, yet county and prefectural levies know no limit."

sentences.zh: 朝廷不能盡擇州縣，則必慎擇督撫。

translations.literal: If the court cannot choose every district and prefecture, it must carefully choose governors-general and governors.
translations.idiomatic: If the court cannot pick every county magistrate, it must choose governors-general and governors with care.

sentences.zh: 督撫不取之屬員，則屬員自無可挾以為恣睢之地。

translations.literal: If governors-general and governors do not take bribes from their subordinates, then subordinates naturally have nothing to rely on as a ground for arbitrary tyranny.
translations.idiomatic: When governors refuse graft from subordinates, those subordinates lose the leverage to tyrannize the people.

sentences.zh: 今日河南積習，祗曰民刁詐，不曰官貪庸；

translations.literal: Today's entrenched habit in Henan is only to call the people crafty and deceitful, not to call officials greedy and incompetent;
translations.idiomatic: Henan's entrenched habit today is to blame crafty, deceitful commoners—not greedy, incompetent officials;

sentences.zh: 祗狃於愚民之抗官，不思所以致抗之由。

translations.literal: it is only fixated on ignorant commoners' resistance to officials, without reflecting on what causes that resistance.
translations.idiomatic: officials fixate on peasants defying authority and never ask what drives that defiance.

sentences.zh: 惟在朝廷慎察大吏，力挽積習，寇亂之源，庶幾可弭。

translations.literal: It lies solely in the court's careful scrutiny of high officials and vigorous reversal of entrenched habits—then the source of banditry and rebellion may perhaps be quelled."
translations.idiomatic: Only if the court scrutinizes its senior appointees and forcefully reverses these habits can the roots of rebellion perhaps be cut."

sentences.zh: 」是年秋，拜文淵閣大學士，疏劾新授廣東巡撫黃贊湯貪詐，解其職。

translations.literal: " That autumn he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Profundity; in a memorial he impeached the newly appointed Governor of Guangdong Huang Zantang for greed and deceit, and [Huang] was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: " That autumn he became grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion; he memorialized against the newly appointed Guangdong governor Huang Zantang for corruption and fraud, and Huang was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 六年，同文館議考選正途五品以下京外官入館肄習天文算學，聘西人為教習。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Tongwen Guan deliberated selecting regular-route officials of the fifth rank and below from the capital and provinces to study in the academy astronomy and mathematics, and hiring Westerners as instructors.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Tongwen Guan proposed enrolling regular-route officials below the fifth rank to study astronomy and mathematics, with Westerners as instructors.

sentences.zh: 倭仁謂根本之圖，在人心不在技藝，尤以西人教習為不可；

translations.literal: Wo Ren said the fundamental plan lay in people's hearts, not in technical skills, and especially that Western instructors were unacceptable;
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren argued that the root remedy lay in men's hearts, not in technical skills, and above all that Western teachers were unacceptable;

sentences.zh: 且謂必習天文算學，應求中國能精其法者，上疏請罷議。

translations.literal: moreover, if astronomy and mathematics must be studied, Chinese who master their methods should be sought; he memorialized the throne asking that the deliberation be halted.
translations.idiomatic: and if such studies were needed, Chinese masters of the methods should be found; he memorialized to stop the plan.

sentences.zh: 於是詔倭仁保薦，別設一館，即由倭仁督率講求。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Wo Ren to recommend [instructors]; a separate academy was to be established, with Wo Ren directing and leading the pursuit of study.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Wo Ren to nominate teachers and set up a separate academy under his direction.

sentences.zh: 復奏意中並無其人，不敢妄保。

translations.literal: He memorialized again that he had no such person in mind and dared not recommend recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: He replied that he knew no one fit for the task and dared not recommend blindly.

sentences.zh: 尋命在總理各國事務衙門行走。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered to serve in the Zongli Yamen for foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to serve in the Zongli Yamen for foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 倭仁屢疏懇辭，不允；

translations.literal: Wo Ren repeatedly memorialized earnestly declining; [his requests] were not granted;
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren repeatedly begged off by memorial; the court refused;

sentences.zh: 因稱疾篤，乞休，命解兼職，仍在弘德殿行走。

translations.literal: thereupon pleading grave illness and requesting retirement; he was ordered to relinquish his concurrent posts but to continue serving in Hongde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: then pleaded serious illness and asked to retire; he was relieved of concurrent posts but kept on duty in Hongde Hall.

sentences.zh: 八年，疏言大婚典禮宜崇節儉，及武英殿災，复偕徐桐、翁同龢疏請勤修聖德，停罷一切工程，以弭災變，並嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized that the grand wedding ceremonies should uphold frugality; when the Hall of Martial Glory burned, he again joined Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe in memorializing to cultivate sagely virtue diligently, halt all construction projects to quell calamitous changes—and [the court] commended and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he urged frugality for the imperial wedding; after fire destroyed the Hall of Martial Glory, he joined Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe in asking the emperor to cultivate virtue and halt all building projects to avert disaster—and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 十年，晉文華殿大學士，以疾再乞休。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and again begged retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to grand secretary of the Wenhua Pavilion and again asked to retire on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太保，入祀賢良祠，諡文端。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died; he was posthumously given the title of Grand Guardian, entered for worship in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and granted the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after; posthumously he was made grand guardian, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and given the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，河南巡撫李鶴年奏建專祠於開封，允之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu, Li Henian, Governor of Henan, memorialized to build a dedicated shrine at Kaifeng; [the request] was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 8 (1882) Henan governor Li Henian asked to erect a private shrine to Wo Ren at Kaifeng; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，曾國籓官京師，與倭仁、李棠階、吳廷棟、何桂珍、竇垿講求宋儒之學。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zeng Guofan held office in the capital, he together with Wo Ren, Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong, He Guizhen, and Dou Kan pursued the learning of Song Neo-Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while Zeng Guofan served in the capital, he studied Song Neo-Confucianism with Wo Ren, Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong, He Guizhen, and Dou Kan.

sentences.zh: 其後國籓出平大難，為中興名臣冠；

translations.literal: Afterward Guofan went out to quell great calamities and stood at the head of the Restoration's famous ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Later Guofan took the field to end the rebellions and became the foremost statesman of the Restoration;

sentences.zh: 倭仁作帝師，正色不阿；

translations.literal: Wo Ren served as the Emperor's teacher, stern in countenance and yielding to none;
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren served as imperial tutor, stern and unbending;

sentences.zh: 棠階、廷棟亦卓然有以自見焉。

translations.literal: Tangjie and Tingdong likewise distinguished themselves in their own right.
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie and Tingdong likewise made their own mark.

sentences.zh: 倭仁著有遺書十三卷。

translations.literal: Wo Ren left posthumous writings in thirteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Ren left thirteen juan of posthumous writings.

sentences.zh: 子福咸，江蘇鹽法道，署安徽徽寧池太廣道，咸豐十年，殉難寧國，贈太僕寺卿，騎都尉世職；

translations.literal: His son Fuxian was Jiangsu salt commissioner, acting intendant of Huining, Chitai, and Taiguang in Anhui; in the tenth year of Xianfeng he died in the line of duty at Ningguo, was posthumously made Vice President of the Court of Imperial Stud, and granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: His son Fuxian served as Jiangsu salt commissioner and acting Anhui intendant; in Xianfeng 10 he was killed at Ningguo, posthumously made vice president of the Court of Imperial Stud, and granted the hereditary rank of commandant of cavalry;

sentences.zh: 福裕，奉天府府尹。

translations.literal: Fuyu was Prefect of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyu was prefect of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 從子福潤，安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: His nephew Furun was Governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Furun became governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十六年，外國兵入京師，闔家死焉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu, when foreign troops entered the capital, the entire family perished.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 26 (1900), when foreign troops entered Beijing, the whole family perished.

sentences.zh: 李棠階，字文園，河南河內人。

translations.literal: Li Tangjie, whose style was Wenyuan, was a native of Henei in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tangjie, styled Wenyuan, was from Henei in Henan.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 (1822) he passed the jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 五遷至侍讀。

translations.literal: After five promotions he reached Expositor-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he reached expositor-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，督廣東學政，擢太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he supervised education in Guangdong and was promoted to Vice President of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he served as Guangdong education commissioner and was promoted to vice president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 會巡撫黃恩彤奏請予鄉試年老武生職銜，嚴旨責譴，棠階亦因違例送考，議降三級調用，遂引疾家居。

translations.literal: When Governor Huang Entong memorialized to grant honorary military titles to elderly military licentiates at the provincial examination, a stern edict rebuked [him]; Tangjie also, for violating regulations in presenting candidates for examination, was deliberated for demotion three ranks and transfer, and thereupon pleaded illness and retired to his home.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Huang Entong asked to grant honorary titles to elderly military candidates at the provincial exams, the court rebuked him sharply; Tangjie too was found to have broken rules in forwarding candidates, was slated for demotion three ranks, and retired home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，复日講，曾國籓薦棠階醇正堪備講官，召來京。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, daily lectures resumed; Zeng Guofan recommended Tangjie as pure and upright and fit to serve as lecturer, and he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor took the throne, daily lectures resumed; Zeng Guofan recommended Tangjie as upright and fit to lecture, and he was summoned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 既而日講中輟，棠階以病未赴。

translations.literal: Before long the daily lectures were suspended, and Tangjie, being ill, did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: The lectures soon lapsed, and Tangjie, citing illness, never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪北犯，河北土寇蜂起，用尚書周祖培薦，命治河北團練。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, Cantonese rebels invaded northward and local bandits rose in swarms in Hebei; on the recommendation of Minister Zhou Zupei, [Tangjie] was ordered to organize militia training in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3, as Taiping forces pushed north and Hebei bandits multiplied, Zhou Zupei recommended Tangjie to organize militia training in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 棠階聯絡村鎮，名曰「友助社」。

translations.literal: Tangjie linked villages and market towns under the name "Society of Mutual Aid."
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie linked villages and towns in an organization he called the Society of Mutual Aid.

sentences.zh: 賊踞溫縣東河灘柳林，四出焚掠，棠階督團練擊之，村民未習戰，且無火器，殺賊數十人，卒不敵。

translations.literal: The bandits occupied the willow groves on the eastern river beach at Wen County and raided in all directions; Tangjie directed the militia to attack them; the villagers were unaccustomed to fighting and had no firearms; they killed several dozen bandits but in the end could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits held the willow groves on Wen County's east river beach and raided widely; Tangjie led the militia against them, but the peasants were untrained and unarmed; they killed dozens of bandits but could not hold.

sentences.zh: 會山東巡撫李僡率兵至，賊引去。

translations.literal: When Li Xin, Governor of Shandong, arrived leading troops, the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong governor Li Xin arrived with troops, the bandits withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賊自渡黃河，始知民間有備，稍稍牽綴。

translations.literal: From the time the bandits crossed the Yellow River, they learned that the populace was prepared and were somewhat held back.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yellow River, the rebels found the countryside armed and their advance slowed.

sentences.zh: 洎河北肅清，敘勞，加四品卿銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: When Hebei was pacified, his merit was recorded; he was given the brevet rank of fourth-rank grand secretary and awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei was cleared, his service was rewarded with a brevet fourth-rank grand secretary title and the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，詔起用舊臣，棠階應召至。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi an edict recalled former ministers to service; Tangjie answered the summons and arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 an edict recalled retired officials; Tangjie answered the call and came to court.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「用人行政，惟在治心。

translations.literal: He memorialized the throne, stating: "In employing men and administering government, everything lies in governing the mind."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Appointments and policy all hinge on governing the mind."

sentences.zh: 治心之要，莫先克己。

translations.literal: The essential of governing the mind is nothing before self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The heart of that discipline is self-restraint above all.

sentences.zh: 請於師保匡弼之馀，豫杜左右近習之漸。

translations.literal: I beg that beyond the teachers and assistants who correct and aid, the gradual encroachment of those close at hand be forestalled in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the tutors who guide you, I ask that you guard early against the gradual influence of court favorites.

sentences.zh: 暇時進講通鑑、大學衍義諸書，以收物格意誠之效。

translations.literal: In leisure hours advance lectures on the Comprehensive Mirror, the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, and such books, to achieve the effect of investigating things and making the will sincere.
translations.idiomatic: In spare hours lecture on the Comprehensive Mirror, the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, and the like, to cultivate sincerity through understanding things.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「紀綱之飭，在於嚴明賞罰。

translations.literal: " He also stated: "The tightening of discipline lies in strict and clear rewards and punishments."
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "Restoring discipline depends on clear rewards and punishments."

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷通諭諸事，務飭疆臣實力奉行，庶中外情志可通，而禍亂可弭。

translations.literal: In all matters of general imperial notification, frontier officials must be ordered to carry them out in earnest, so that sentiment within and without may communicate and calamity and rebellion may be quelled."
translations.idiomatic: Every imperial order must be enforced in earnest by frontier officials, so that court and provinces stay aligned and rebellion may be quelled."

sentences.zh: 」兩宮嘉納焉。

translations.literal: " The two palaces commended and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowagers approved.

sentences.zh: 授大理寺卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed President of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 先是兩江總督何桂清僨事逮治，部讞從重擬斬決，廷臣有右之者，言部臣有意畸重，仍從本律監候。

translations.literal: Earlier, He Guiqing, Governor-General of the Two Jiangs, had been arrested and tried for losing his post; the ministry's deliberation proposed execution by decapitation with aggravation; some court ministers supported him, saying the ministry intentionally weighed the penalty too heavily, and [the sentence] still followed the statute for imprisonment awaiting execution.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Two Jiangs governor-general He Guiqing had been arrested for abandoning his post; the ministry recommended aggravated decapitation; some courtiers defended him, arguing the ministry had overreached, and the sentence was reduced to imprisonment awaiting execution.

sentences.zh: 棠階疏謂桂清貽誤封疆罪大，不當輕比，非公論。

translations.literal: Tangjie memorialized that Guiqing's crime of bringing disaster on the frontier was grave and should not be lightly compared [to lesser offenses]; this was not public justice.
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie memorialized that Guiqing's crime of abandoning the frontier was grave and should not be softened—that would not be justice.

sentences.zh: 後桂清卒伏法。

translations.literal: Later Guiqing in the end suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing was eventually executed.

sentences.zh: 連擢禮部侍郎、左都御史，署戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Vice President of the Ministry of Rites and Left Censor-in-Chief, and acted as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to vice president of rites and left censor-in-chief, and served as acting minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 召對，言：「治天下惟在安民，安民必先察吏。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he said: "Governing the realm lies solely in settling the people; settling the people must begin with scrutinizing officials."
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, he said: "Governing the realm means settling the people, and that begins with scrutinizing officials."

sentences.zh: 今日之盜賊，即昔日之良民，皆地方有司貪虐激之成變。

translations.literal: Today's bandits are yesterday's law-abiding people—all stirred to revolt by the greed and cruelty of local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Today's rebels were yesterday's law-abiding subjects, every one driven to revolt by greedy, brutal local officials.

sentences.zh: 為今日平亂計，非輕徭薄賦不能治本。

translations.literal: For the plan to pacify disorder today, light taxes and reduced levies alone can remedy the root.
translations.idiomatic: To pacify the realm today, nothing remedies the root like light taxes and reduced levies.

sentences.zh: 然非擇大吏，則守令不得其人，亦終不能收令行禁止之效。

translations.literal: Yet unless great officials are chosen, prefects and magistrates will not be the right men, and in the end the effect of orders enforced and prohibitions heeded cannot be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: But without choosing the right senior appointees, magistrates will remain unfit, and orders will never truly be obeyed.

sentences.zh: 」因極言河南亂事，及諸行省利病甚悉。

translations.literal: Therefore he spoke at length on the turmoil in Henan and the advantages and harms of the various provinces in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: He went on at length about unrest in Henan and the strengths and weaknesses of every province.

sentences.zh: 命為軍機大臣，具疏力辭，弗許。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Councilor; he memorialized earnestly declining but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand councilor; he memorialized earnestly to decline, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 二年，授工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 三年，江寧克復，論功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Nanjing was recovered, his merit was reckoned and he was given the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Nanjing was recovered, his merit was rewarded with the title junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 大憝既平，上諭中外臣工以兢業交勉。

translations.literal: With the great enemy already pacified, the Emperor instructed civil and military officials within and without to encourage one another in vigilance and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: With the great rebellion crushed, the emperor urged officials everywhere to encourage one another in diligence and vigilance.

sentences.zh: 棠階語恭親王及同直諸大臣，謂當設誠致行，久而不懈，勿徒以空言相文飾，王深然之。

translations.literal: Tangjie spoke to Prince Gong and the other Grand Councilors on duty, saying they should establish sincerity and act accordingly, long without slackening, and not merely ornament things with empty words; the Prince deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Tangjie told Prince Gong and his fellow councilors that the court must act in earnest and persevere—not trade in empty words; the prince strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 翼日召對，王反复陳君臣交儆之義，棠階與同僚繼言之，兩宮改容嘉納。

translations.literal: The next day, summoned for audience, the Prince repeatedly set forth the meaning of mutual vigilance between ruler and minister; Tangjie and his colleagues spoke further; the two palaces changed expression and commended and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The next day at audience the prince repeated the theme of mutual vigilance between ruler and ministers; Tangjie and colleagues spoke further; the empress dowagers visibly approved.

sentences.zh: 尋調禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 太后命南書房、上書房諸臣纂輯前史事蹟，賜名治平寶鑑，命諸大臣進講。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered the members of the Southern Study and Upper Study to compile historical deeds of former ages, bestowed the title Mirror of Ordered Peace, and ordered the great ministers to advance in lecturing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered scholars of the Southern and Upper Studies to compile historical precedents, named the work Mirror of Ordered Peace, and charged senior ministers to lecture on it.

sentences.zh: 棠階因講漢文帝卻千里馬事，反复推言人主不宜有所嗜好，以啟窺伺之端。

translations.literal: Tangjie, in lecturing on Emperor Wen of Han's rejection of horses from a thousand leagues, repeatedly argued that the sovereign ought not to have any particular fondness, lest it open a point for those who spy and scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturing on Emperor Wen of Han rejecting tribute horses, Tangjie argued that a ruler must avoid personal indulgences that invite courtiers to pry and scheme.

sentences.zh: 自是每進講必原本經義，極論史事，歸於責難陳善。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever he lectured he always grounded himself in canonical meaning, discussed historical affairs to the utmost, and concluded with admonition and presentation of what is good.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every lecture grounded itself in the classics, drew moral lessons from history, and ended in frank admonition.

sentences.zh: 四年，恭親王被劾退出軍機，棠階謂王有定難功，時方多故，不當輕棄親賢，入對，力言王非有心之失。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Prince Gong was impeached and removed from the Grand Council; Tangjie said the Prince had merit in settling the crisis, and with affairs momentarily numerous, close and worthy kin should not lightly be cast aside; entering audience, he strongly stated that the Prince's fault was not intentional.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Prince Gong was impeached and removed from the Grand Council; Tangjie said the prince had saved the dynasty and that in troubled times close royal kin should not be cast aside; at audience he insisted the fault was not deliberate.

sentences.zh: 會惇、醇兩王亦奏言奕訢不可遽罷，乃復命入直。

translations.literal: When the Princes of Dun and Chun also memorialized that Yixin should not be hastily dismissed, [the Emperor] again ordered him to serve on duty.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes of Dun and Chun also urged that Yixin not be dismissed hastily, the emperor ordered him back to the council.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁戰歿曹州，棠階以朝廷賞多罰少，疆臣每存藐玩，上疏極言其弊，於是有申飭直省督撫之諭。

translations.literal: When Sengge Rinchen fell in battle at Caozhou, Tangjie, because the court rewarded much and punished little and frontier great officials often held things in contempt, memorialized strongly on these evils; thereupon came an edict sternly admonishing governors-general and governors of the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After Sengge Rinchen died at Caozhou, Tangjie memorialized that rewards outweighed punishments and frontier governors grew contemptuous; the court issued a stern edict admonishing provincial governors.

sentences.zh: 棠階自入直樞廷，軍書旁午，一事稍有未安，輒憂形於色。

translations.literal: From the time Tangjie entered service in the Grand Council, military documents poured in from all sides; whenever anything was slightly unsettled, worry showed in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the Grand Council, with military dispatches pouring in, the slightest setback showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 積勞致疾，十一月，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: Accumulated exertion brought on illness; in the eleventh month he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Overwork brought on illness; in the eleventh month he died, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 上震悼，遣貝勒載治奠醊，賜金治喪，贈太子太保，諡文清。

translations.literal: The Emperor was shaken and grieved; he dispatched Prince Zaiye to offer libations, bestowed gold for the funeral, posthumously made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and granted the posthumous name Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved; he sent Prince Zaiye to offer libations, granted gold for the funeral, posthumously made him junior guardian of the heir apparent, and gave him the posthumous name Wenqing.

sentences.zh: 棠階初入翰林，即潛心理學，嘗手鈔湯斌遺書以自勗。

translations.literal: When Tangjie first entered the Hanlin, he secretly devoted himself to Neo-Confucian learning and once copied by hand Tang Bin's posthumous writings to exhort himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Tangjie first entered the Hanlin, he devoted himself to Neo-Confucianism and copied Tang Bin's posthumous writings by hand to exhort himself.

sentences.zh: 會通程、硃、陸、王學說，無所偏主，要以克己復禮、身體實行為歸。

translations.literal: Having mastered the doctrines of the Cheng-Zhu and Lu-Wang schools without partiality, he took self-restraint and return to propriety and earnest personal practice as his aim.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Cheng-Zhu and Lu-Wang schools without partiality, aiming at self-restraint, return to propriety, and earnest practice.

sentences.zh: 日記自省，畢生不懈。

translations.literal: He examined himself in a daily diary, never slackening through his whole life.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a diary of self-examination and never slackened throughout his life.

sentences.zh: 家故貧，既貴，儉約無改。

translations.literal: His family had long been poor; once he achieved eminence, he remained thrifty and sparing without change.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been poor; even after rising high, he remained as thrifty as before.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「憂患者生之門。

translations.literal: He once said: "Affliction is the gateway to life."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Affliction is the gateway to life."

sentences.zh: 吾終身不敢忘忍飢待米時也！

translations.literal: I dare never in my whole life forget the time when I endured hunger waiting for rice!"
translations.idiomatic: I shall never forget going hungry while waiting for rice!"

sentences.zh: 吳廷棟，字竹如，安徽霍山人。

translations.literal: Wu Tingdong, whose style was Zhuru, was a native of Huoshan in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingdong, styled Zhuru, was from Huoshan in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光五年拔貢，授刑部七品小京官，洊遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daoguang he was selected as a tribute student, appointed a seventh-rank junior secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, and gradually promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 5 (1825) he was selected as a tribute student, appointed a seventh-rank secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 廷棟少好宋儒之學，入官益植節厲行，蹇蹇自靖。

translations.literal: Tingdong from youth loved Song Neo-Confucian learning; upon entering office he further cultivated integrity and stern conduct, cautious and self-restrained.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tingdong loved Song Neo-Confucianism; in office he cultivated integrity and stern, cautious conduct.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，京察一等。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was graded first class in the capital inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 he received the top grade in the capital personnel review.

sentences.zh: 時侍郎書元兼崇文門副監督，獲販私釀者三十六人，承審者以漏稅擬滿杖。

translations.literal: At that time Vice President Shu Yuan concurrently served as deputy supervisor of the Chongwen Gate and apprehended thirty-six persons smuggling private brew; those conducting the trial proposed the full bamboo punishment for tax evasion.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice President Shu Yuan, deputy supervisor of the Chongwen Gate, seized thirty-six smugglers of illicit liquor, the trial officers proposed the full statutory bamboo punishment for tax evasion.

sentences.zh: 已而覆訊得書元家人詐贓狀，部臣據以入奏。

translations.literal: Later, upon re-examination, the fact that Shu's family members extorted bribes was obtained, and the ministry officials memorialized accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: On re-examination it emerged that Shu's family had extorted bribes, and the ministry memorialized accordingly.

sentences.zh: 文宗疑書元孤立，降旨切責，會廷棟召對，上詢是獄。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong suspected Shu was isolated; he issued an edict sharply rebuking [the ministry]; when Tingdong was summoned for audience, the Emperor inquired about the case.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianfeng Emperor suspected Shu was being isolated and rebuked the ministry sharply; when Tingdong was summoned, the emperor asked about the case.

sentences.zh: 廷棟從容敷奏，且詳陳治道之要，言利之害，君子小人之辨，上首肯，獄竟得解。

translations.literal: Tingdong calmly explained and in detail set forth essentials of governance, the harm of profit-seeking, and the distinction between gentlemen and petty men; the Emperor nodded assent, and the case was finally resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong explained calmly, setting forth the essentials of governance, the harm of profit-seeking, and the distinction between gentlemen and petty men; the emperor nodded assent, and the case was resolved.

sentences.zh: 因詢廷棟讀何書，廷棟以程、硃對。

translations.literal: Thereupon he asked what books Tingdong read; Tingdong answered Cheng and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked what Tingdong read; Tingdong answered, the Cheng-Zhu school.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「學程、硃者每多迂拘。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Those who study Cheng and Zhu are often narrow and rigid."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Students of Cheng and Zhu are often narrow and rigid."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此不善學之過。

translations.literal: He replied: "That is the fault of poor study."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "That is the fault of poor study."

sentences.zh: 程、硃以明德為體，新民為用，天下未有有體而無用者。

translations.literal: Cheng and Zhu take illustrious virtue as substance and renewing the people as function; in the realm there is none who has substance without function.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Zhu take illustrious virtue as substance and renewing the people as function; nothing in the world has substance without function.

sentences.zh: 皇上讀書窮理，以裕知人之識；

translations.literal: Your Majesty, in reading books and exhausting principle, may enlarge the knowledge by which men are discerned;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty reads to exhaust principle, you will enlarge your knowledge for discerning men;

sentences.zh: 清心寡欲，以養坐照之明。

translations.literal: in clearing the mind and few desires, may nurture the clarity of seated illumination.
translations.idiomatic: if you clear the mind and limit desires, you will nurture the clarity of insight.

sentences.zh: 寤寐求賢，內外得人，天下何憂不治？

translations.literal: Seeking worthies waking and sleeping, obtaining men within and without—what worry is there that the realm cannot be governed?
translations.idiomatic: Seek worthies waking and sleeping, gain good men within and without—why should the realm not be governed?

sentences.zh: 」上韙之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋出為直隸河間知府。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he went out as Prefect of Hejian in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as prefect of Hejian in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 粵匪北犯畿輔，廷棟練民兵巡防，民倚以為固。

translations.literal: When Cantonese rebels invaded north toward the capital region, Tingdong trained militia for patrol and defense, and the people relied on him as a bulwark.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping rebels pushed toward the capital region, Tingdong trained militia for patrol and defense, and the people relied on him as their bulwark.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士勝保督師至河間，責供張甚急，知縣王灴迫於應付，自刎不殊。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Sengge Ba supervised the army to Hejian and urgently demanded supplies; Magistrate Wang Hong, pressed in meeting the demand, attempted suicide but did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Sheng Bao led troops to Hejian and demanded supplies urgently; Magistrate Wang Hong, unable to meet the demand, attempted suicide but survived.

sentences.zh: 廷棟詣大營陳其事，勝保矍然，飭部下聽命。

translations.literal: Tingdong went to the great headquarters and stated the matter; Sengge Ba was startled and ordered his subordinates to obey commands.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong went to headquarters and reported the matter; Sheng Bao was startled and ordered his men to obey.

sentences.zh: 連擢永定河道、直隸按察使。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Commissioner of the Yongding River and Surveillance Commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to commissioner of the Yongding River and surveillance commissioner of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 以河間京師門戶，廷棟善守禦，得民心，仍留知府任。

translations.literal: Because Hejian was the gateway to the capital, Tingdong was skilled in defense, won the people's hearts, and was still kept in the prefect's post.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hejian guarded the capital approaches and Tingdong defended well and won the people's hearts, he was kept in the prefect's post.

sentences.zh: 四年，軍事定，乃之按察使任。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when military affairs were settled, he then took up the surveillance commissioner's post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when military affairs settled, he took up the surveillance commissioner's post.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷山東布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Financial Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to financial commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 時部臣奏請畿內賦稅兼收大錢鈔票各三成，上下交病，總督譚廷襄不敢言。

translations.literal: At that time ministry officials memorialized that taxes within the capital region should collect thirty percent each in large cash, bank notes, and [other forms]; superiors and inferiors alike suffered; Governor-General Tan Tingxiang dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry officials proposed that taxes in the capital region accept thirty percent each in large cash, bank notes, and copper cash; everyone suffered; Governor-General Tan Tingxiang dared not object.

sentences.zh: 會廷棟入覲，面奏：「大錢鈔票實不流通。

translations.literal: When Tingdong came to audience, he stated face to face: "Large cash and bank notes truly do not circulate."
translations.idiomatic: At audience Tingdong stated face to face, "Large cash and bank notes truly do not circulate."

sentences.zh: 立法必先便於民方可行，必先信於民方能久。

translations.literal: In making laws one must first make them convenient for the people before they can be carried out; one must first win the people's trust before they can last long.
translations.idiomatic: Laws must first benefit the people before they can work; they must first win the people's trust before they can endure.

sentences.zh: 今條科太多，朝夕更改，國家先不能自信，何以取信於民？

translations.literal: Today there are too many tax items, changed morning and evening; if the state itself cannot have confidence, how can it win the people's trust?
translations.idiomatic: Today tax items multiply and change from day to day; if the state lacks confidence in its own laws, how can the people trust them?

sentences.zh: 」上首肯者再。

translations.literal: The Emperor nodded assent twice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded assent twice.

sentences.zh: 既而廷襄入朝，遂奏罷前議。

translations.literal: Later when Tingxiang came to court, he then memorialized to halt the previous proposal.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan Tingxiang came to court, he memorialized to halt the proposal.

sentences.zh: 山東吏治久窳，廷棟獎廉懲貪。

translations.literal: Shandong administration had long been corrupt; Tingdong rewarded integrity and punished greed.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong administration had long been corrupt; Tingdong rewarded the honest and punished the greedy.

sentences.zh: 方議海口立局收貨捐，持不可。

translations.literal: When they were deliberating establishing a bureau at the estuary to levy donations on goods, he opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: When officials proposed a customs bureau at the estuary to levy transit dues, he opposed it.

sentences.zh: 八年，坐奏銷遲誤，降補直隸按察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, for delayed reporting and clearance of accounts, he was demoted and reassigned as Surveillance Commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, for delayed account clearance, he was demoted to surveillance commissioner of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復調山東。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was again transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred back to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，入為大理寺卿，尋擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he entered [the capital] as President of the Court of Judicial Review and soon was promoted to Vice President of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 2 he entered the capital as president of the Court of Judicial Review and was soon promoted to vice president of punishments.

sentences.zh: 三年，江南平，廷棟上疏，略曰：「萬方之治亂在朝政，百工之敬肆視君心。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Jiangnan was pacified, Tingdong memorialized, stating in summary: "Order and disorder throughout the realm lie in court governance; the diligence or laxity of the hundred officials depends on the ruler's mind."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Jiangnan was pacified, Tingdong memorialized in essence: "Whether the realm is ordered or chaotic depends on court governance; whether officials are diligent or lax depends on the ruler's mind."

sentences.zh: 事不貴文，貴其實；

translations.literal: Affairs are not prized for ornament but for their substance;
translations.idiomatic: Affairs should be valued for substance, not ornament;

sentences.zh: 下不從令，從所好。

translations.literal: inferiors do not follow orders but follow what [the ruler] favors.
translations.idiomatic: subordinates do not follow orders—they follow what the ruler favors.

sentences.zh: 夫治亂決於敬肆，敬肆根於喜懼。

translations.literal: Order and disorder are decided by reverence or laxity; reverence and laxity root in joy or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Order and disorder turn on reverence or laxity; reverence and laxity root in joy or fear.

sentences.zh: 自古功成志遂，人主喜心一生而驕心已伏，宦寺有乘其喜而貢諂媚者矣，左右有乘其喜而肆蒙蔽者矣，容悅之臣有因此而工諛佞者矣，屏逐之姦有因此而巧夤緣者矣。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, when success is achieved and ambitions fulfilled, joy arises in the ruler's heart and pride is already hidden; eunuchs take advantage of joy to offer flattery; those at the ruler's side take advantage of joy to deceive and conceal; ministers who please take this occasion to craft flattery; dismissed villains take this occasion to scheme connections by artifice.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, when success is won and ambitions fulfilled, joy enters the ruler's heart and pride lies hidden; eunuchs use joy to offer flattery; attendants use joy to deceive; sycophants use it to perfect their craft; disgraced schemers use it to claw back favor.

sentences.zh: 諂媚貢則柄暗竊，蒙蔽肆則權下移，諛佞工則主志惑，夤緣巧則宵小升。

translations.literal: When flattery is offered, power is secretly usurped; when deception runs riot, authority shifts downward; when flattery is crafted, the ruler's will is confused; when scheming connections are artful, base men rise.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery secretly usurps power; deception shifts authority downward; sycophancy confuses the ruler's will; scheming elevates base men.

sentences.zh: 於是受蠱惑，塞聰明，遠老成，惡忠鯁。

translations.literal: Thereupon one accepts bewitchment, blocks keen hearing, distances the mature, and hates loyal bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: Then the ruler accepts delusion, blocks his ears, distances the mature, and hates blunt loyalty.

sentences.zh: 從前戒懼之念，一喜敗之；

translations.literal: The former thoughts of vigilance and fear are ruined by a single joy;
translations.idiomatic: Former vigilance and fear are undone by a single burst of joy;

sentences.zh: 此後侈縱之行，一喜開之。

translations.literal: thereafter the conduct of extravagance and indulgence is opened by a single joy.
translations.idiomatic: thereafter extravagance and indulgence are opened by that same joy.

sentences.zh: 方且矜予智，樂莫違，逞獨斷，快從欲，一人肆於上，群小扇於下，流毒蒼生，貽禍社稷，稽諸史冊，後先一轍。

translations.literal: One prides oneself on one's wisdom, delights in none disobeying, indulges in arbitrary decisions, gratifies desires—a single person unrestrained above, a host of petty men fanning below, poisoning the black-haired people and leaving calamity to the altars of soil and grain; consulted in historical annals, early and late follow the same track.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler prides himself on wisdom, delights when none disobey, indulges arbitrary decisions and every desire—one man unrestrained above, petty men fanning below, poisoning the people and endangering the state; history shows the same pattern again and again.

sentences.zh: 推原其端，祗一念由喜入驕而已。

translations.literal: Tracing to the origin, it is only a single thought entering pride from joy.
translations.idiomatic: Trace it to the root, and it is only a single thought of joy turning to pride.

sentences.zh: 軍興以來，十數省億萬生靈慘遭鋒鏑，即倡亂之奸民，何一非朝廷赤子？

translations.literal: Since military campaigns began, hundreds of millions of living beings in a dozen-odd provinces have suffered cruelly from sword and spear; even the villainous commoners who raised rebellion—were they not every one the court's own children?
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, hundreds of millions in a dozen provinces have suffered under arms; even the rebels who rose—were they not the court's own children?

sentences.zh: 大兵所加，盡被誅夷。

translations.literal: Where great armies struck, all were slaughtered and exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Where imperial armies struck, all were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 皇太后、皇上體上天好生之心，必有哀矜不忍喜者。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager and Emperor, embodying Heaven's mind to cherish life, must surely have compassion and forbearance, not joy.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and emperor, embodying Heaven's love of life, must feel compassion, not joy.

sentences.zh: 況旗兵乏食，根本空虛，新疆缺餉，邊陲搖動。

translations.literal: Moreover banner troops lack food, the foundation is hollow, Xinjiang lacks pay, and the frontier shakes.
translations.idiomatic: Banner troops lack food, the dynasty's foundation is hollow, Xinjiang lacks pay, and the frontier trembles.

sentences.zh: 兼之強鄰偪處，邪教肆行，豈惟不可喜，而實屬可懼。

translations.literal: In addition powerful neighbors press close and heterodox sects run riot—not only may one not rejoice, but it is truly a matter for fear.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful neighbors press close and heterodox sects run wild—not only is there no cause for joy, but there is real cause for fear.

sentences.zh: 假使萬幾之馀，或有一念之肆，臣工效之，視彰癉為故事，輕告戒為具文，積習相沿，工為粉飾，將仍成為叢脞怠荒之局矣。

translations.literal: Suppose amid the myriad affairs there is a single thought of indulgence copied by officials, who treat rewards and punishments as routine and lightly regard admonitions as empty documents, habits accumulating and craftsmen of whitewash at work—then again the pattern of confusion, triviality, sluggishness, and neglect will be formed.
translations.idiomatic: If amid myriad affairs a single indulgent thought spreads, if officials treat rewards and punishments as routine and admonitions as empty words, if habit piles on habit and whitewash prevails—the old pattern of confusion and neglect returns.

sentences.zh: 是非堅定刻苦，持之以恆，積數十年恭儉憂勤，有未易培國脈復元氣者。

translations.literal: Unless one is firm, painstaking, and perseveres with constancy for several decades in reverence, frugality, worry, and diligence, it is not easy to nurture the nation's pulse and restore its vital energy.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the ruler is firm, painstaking, and for decades perseveres in reverence, frugality, worry, and diligence, it is hard to restore the nation's vital strength.

sentences.zh: 夫上行必下效，內治則外安，而其道莫大於敬，其幾必始於懼。

translations.literal: Superiors must be followed by inferiors; inner governance then outer peace—and its Way is nothing greater than reverence, its subtle beginning necessarily in fear.
translations.idiomatic: What superiors do, inferiors follow; inner order brings outer peace—and the greatest Way is reverence, whose subtle beginning is fear.

sentences.zh: 懼天命無常，則不敢恃天；

translations.literal: Fear that Heaven's mandate is inconstant, then one dare not rely on Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Fear Heaven's mandate is inconstant, and one dare not rely on Heaven;

sentences.zh: 懼民碞可畏，則不敢玩民。

translations.literal: fear that the people's anger is formidable, then one dare not toy with the people.
translations.idiomatic: fear the people's anger is formidable, and one dare not toy with the people.

sentences.zh: 懼者敬之始，敬者懼之終。

translations.literal: Fear is the beginning of reverence; reverence is the end of fear.
translations.idiomatic: Fear is the beginning of reverence; reverence is the end of fear.

sentences.zh: 大智愈明，神武愈彰，紹祖宗富有之大業，開子孫無疆之丕基，是皆由皇心之懼始而敬成也。

translations.literal: Greater wisdom grows clearer, martial spirit grows more manifest, continuing the ancestors' rich enterprise, opening boundless foundation for sons and grandsons—all begin from the sovereign heart's fear and are completed in reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Greater wisdom grows clearer, martial spirit more manifest, the ancestors' rich enterprise continued, boundless foundation opened for posterity—all begin in the sovereign's fear and are completed in reverence.

sentences.zh: 易曰：'危者使平，易者使傾，懼以終始，其要無咎。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: 'In peril one seeks peace; in ease one invites overturning; with fear from beginning to end, the key is no blame.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "In peril one seeks peace; in ease one invites ruin; with fear from beginning to end, the key is no blame."

sentences.zh: '詩曰：'敬之敬之，天維顯思！

translations.literal: The Book of Odes says: 'Reverent, reverent—Heaven clearly considers!'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, "Reverent, reverent—Heaven clearly sees!"

sentences.zh: '可弗以為永鑑歟？

translations.literal: May this not serve as an eternal mirror?
translations.idiomatic: May this not serve as an eternal mirror?

sentences.zh: 」疏上，優詔嘉納，命存其疏於弘​​德殿以備省覽。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an excellent edict commended and accepted it, ordering the memorial kept in Hongde Hall for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, an excellent edict approved it and ordered it kept in Hongde Hall for the emperor's review.

sentences.zh: 皇太后召對時，諭曰：「皇帝衝齡踐阼，國家大事，汝宜直言無隱，以無負先帝知遇。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager summoned him for audience, she instructed: "The Emperor at tender years has ascended the throne; on great affairs of state you should speak frankly without concealment, lest you fail the late Emperor's gracious trust."
translations.idiomatic: At audience the empress dowager said, "The emperor is young; on great affairs speak frankly and hold nothing back, lest you fail the late emperor's trust."

sentences.zh: 」廷棟感激出涕。

translations.literal: Tingdong, moved, wept.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong wept with emotion.

sentences.zh: 五年，以衰病乞休，許之，歸寓江寧。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on grounds of decline and illness he begged retirement; it was granted, and he returned to lodge in Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he begged retirement on grounds of age and illness; permission was granted, and he settled in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒，年八十有一。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died, aged eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 遺疏入，詔褒其廉靜自持，賜卹如例。

translations.literal: When his final memorial arrived, an edict praised his holding himself in integrity and quiet, and bestowed condolence according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial arrived, an edict praised his integrity and quiet conduct and granted condolence as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 直隸、山東皆祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Both Zhili and Shandong enshrined him in shrines of famous officials.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zhili and Shandong enshrined him in their shrines of notable officials.

sentences.zh: 廷棟學以不欺為本。

translations.literal: Tingdong took not deceiving as the root of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong took honesty as the root of learning.

sentences.zh: 官臬司時，畿輔連有逆倫獄，總督慮一月頻入奏幹上怒，廷棟曰：「此吾儕不能教化之過，待罪不暇，敢欺飾耶？

translations.literal: When he was surveillance commissioner, the capital region had successive cases of violation of human relations; the governor-general feared frequent memorials to the throne in one month would anger the sovereign; Tingdong said: "This is our failure to teach and transform; we await punishment—how dare we deceive and cover up?"
translations.idiomatic: As surveillance commissioner, when the capital region saw successive cases of parricide and the governor-general feared frequent memorials would anger the throne, Tingdong said, "This is our failure to teach and transform—we await punishment; how dare we cover it up?"

sentences.zh: 」及去官，僑居清貧，不受餽遺。

translations.literal: After leaving office he lived as a guest in poverty and clean circumstances, accepting no gifts.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he lived in honest poverty as a guest, accepting no gifts.

sentences.zh: 著有拙修集十卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Collected Plain Cultivation in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Collected Plain Cultivation in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 論曰：倭仁晚為兩宮所敬禮，際會中興，輔導衝主，兢兢於君心敬肆之間，當時舉朝嚴憚，風氣賴以維持。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Wo Ren in his later years was revered and honored by the two palaces; encountering the Restoration, he assisted and guided the young ruler, diligently [watching] between reverence and laxity in the ruler's heart; at the time the whole court stood in awe, and the moral climate was maintained thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Wo Ren in his later years was revered by the two empress dowagers; in the Restoration he tutored the young emperor, ever watchful over reverence and laxity in the ruler's heart; the whole court stood in awe of him, and public morals were sustained.

sentences.zh: 惟未達世變，於自強要政，鄙夷不屑言，後轉為異論者所藉口。

translations.literal: Only he did not comprehend the changes of the age; toward essential policies of self-strengthening he showed contempt and disdained to speak, and this later became a handle for those of divergent views.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he failed to grasp the changing times; he scorned the policies of self-strengthening and would not speak of them, giving later critics their chief argument against him.

sentences.zh: 李棠階、吳廷棟正色立朝，不負所學，翕然笙磬同音，而棠階尤平實持大體，可謂體用兼備矣。

translations.literal: Li Tangjie and Wu Tingdong stood in the court with stern countenance, not betraying their learning; like pipes and chimes in harmonious sound—and Tangjie especially was plain and solid in holding to the larger pattern, which may be called having both substance and function complete.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tangjie and Wu Tingdong served with stern integrity true to their learning, moving in concert like matched instruments—and Tangjie especially was plain, steady, and held to the larger pattern, embodying both substance and practice.
